A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and the renamed methods and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original graph-embedding benchmarks on eight datasets, a synthetic stochastic-block-model experiment, and temperature, initialization, and normalization analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds link-prediction, global-distance, and two-hop-neighborhood evaluation results.

M1.justification: The reported initialization changes from Laplacian Eigenmaps to Diffusion Maps in Sections 4.2–4.3. Otherwise, the graph affinities, embedding objectives, and learned-temperature variant are retained; graph NE primarily unifies and renames the existing graph CNE and graph t-SNE approaches.

E1.justification: The eight benchmark graphs and synthetic stochastic-block-model scenario are retained. V2 adds an edge/non-edge ranking task on the existing graphs through its link-prediction evaluation in Appendix B; it adds no new dataset or domain.

E2.justification: The principal accuracy and recall comparator sets are unchanged. V2 adds Laplacian Eigenmaps to the runtime comparison in Figure S1 and reports a qualitative comparison with Diffusion Maps in Section 7.2, finding results similar to Laplacian Eigenmaps.

E3.justification: V2 substantially broadens evaluation with link-prediction AUC using 10% of edges and equally many non-edges, shortest-path distance correlation using 1,000 node pairs, and top-10 two-hop recall. It also changes the stated classification neighborhood from k = 10 to k = 15 and revises the stated initialization. These protocol descriptions do not establish that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds analyses testing preservation of shared-neighbor relationships and global graph distances, exposing properties beyond immediate-neighbor preservation (Tables S5–S6). The earlier temperature experiment, initialization/normalization comparison, and node2vec parameter sweep remain; their relocation does not constitute new analysis.

E5.justification: The existing three-run mean-and-standard-deviation reporting remains. Table S7 newly reports learned-temperature means across three runs and states that their standard deviations are below 0.0005, whereas v1 supplied only the overall temperature range. No increase in run count is established.

E6.justification: Table 2 and Tables S1–S3 retain their numerical results after renaming and reordering. New Tables S4–S7 report link-prediction AUC, global-distance correlations, two-hop recall, and dataset-specific learned temperatures. For example, the new 128D Photo two-hop results favor node2vec over graph NE, 30.9% versus 27.2%. Some individual layout annotations also change between v1 Figure S4 and v2 Figure S3.

T1.justification: V2 adds Theorem 4.1 and an Appendix A proof relating InfoNCE and KL-divergence minimizers under explicit symmetry, connectivity, and exact-representability assumptions. V1 contained no corresponding theorem or proof. Appendices B–C additionally derive a recall–accuracy relationship for regular graphs and formally define the two-hop recall metric.

C1.justification: The central claims of superior local-structure preservation and a unified neighbor-embedding framework remain. V2's discussion additionally claims that both backends scale linearly with the number of graph edges and achieve competitive large-graph runtimes, modestly extending the efficiency claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds a local-versus-global preservation interpretation for the 2D results, explains its preference for neighbor recall over nearly saturated link-prediction AUC, and acknowledges slower small-graph runtimes and inability to embed previously unseen nodes. The earlier temperature/classification trade-off and exclusion of planar and mesh graphs remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds Python usage examples, identifies cne version 0.4.0 and associated API additions, and documents improvements to openTSNE spectral initialization. The reported code repository changes from contrastive-graphs to graph-ne-paper. Most optimizer, training-budget, preprocessing, and hardware information was already present.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussions of IGEL, diffusion and multidimensional-scaling graph methods, Ma and Collins's theoretical work, recent fast tsNET/UMAP approaches, and the usefulness of node features versus edges. These extend the related-work coverage while retaining the central positioning against random-walk embeddings and existing graph layouts.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion are extensively rewritten around graph NE. High-dimensional embeddings now precede 2D layouts in the method and benchmarking sections, terminology changes throughout, and the appendix is reorganized into theory, evaluation definitions, and supplementary results.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column conference layout to a single-column journal layout. Figure 1 is redrawn with color-coded forces, Figure 2's panels are rearranged, plots and table blocks are reordered, and four supplementary tables are added. Earlier supplementary Figures S2–S4 survive as S4, S2, and S3, with revised presentation.

improvement.justification: V2's complementary structural evaluations and implementation examples make the paper more informative and reproducible, particularly by exposing the 2D local-versus-global trade-off in Table S5. These gains are tempered by unresolved issues: Table S2 remains numerically identical despite the stated kNN setting changing from 10 to 15, and Section 4.4 does not justify its exact-representability assumption for the stated graph embeddings. The added evidence and practical guidance support a limited net improvement.
